translationRepairs: In Zhizheng 11 (1351) he was made administrator of Jining Circuit and, by imperial command, marched with the Jiang-Zhe chief minister Jiaohua to relieve Anfeng; at Dinglin Station near Hefei his troops met the rebels and routed them decisively.

In Zhizheng 11 (1351) he was made administrator of Jining Circuit and, by imperial command, marched with the Jiang-Zhe chief minister Jiaohua to advance on Anfeng; at Dinglin Station near Hefei his troops met the rebels and routed them decisively.
徵進安豐 means to campaign against / advance on Anfeng; 'relieve' invents a relief mission absent from the Chinese.
when they see an opening, they are to wave the flags they hold."
when you see an opening, wave the flags you hold.
伺其有間 continues the order to the flag-bearers; the opening is the enemy's gap, not something the bandits themselves notice before waving.
Tuanxiao learned of this and spoke to Zhen about it; Li was immediately exposed as a corpse in the marketplace, and then great rain fell.
Tuanxiao learned of this and spoke to Zhen about it; Zhen at once had him executed and his corpse exposed in the marketplace, and then great rain fell.
即以屍諸市中 implies Zhen ordered execution and public corpse display after the report; the proposed brackets around Zhen are unnecessary in literal English.
Tuanxiao took his post on the wall and sent cavalry out through all four gates to strike the rebel rear, with orders to return at a single wave of the flag."
Tuanxiao took his post on the wall and sent cavalry out through all four gates to strike the rebel rear, ordering them, "Return at a single wave of the flag."
The Chinese presents the instruction as direct speech, so the English should retain Tuanxiao's quoted order while removing the stray unmatched mark.
Envious rivals slandered him to Grand Marshal Niutachai, who ordered him to leave Jinan and rejoin Bolanxi's campaign against Yidu as originally commanded.
Envious rivals slandered him to Grand Marshal Niutachai, who ordered Tuanxiao, in accordance with the former edict, to follow Bolanxi in jointly campaigning against Yidu.
令摶霄依前詔，從卜蘭奚同徵益都 orders following Bolanxi against Yidu per the former edict; departure from Jinan appears only in the next unit.

When news of his death reached the court, he was posthumously honored as Duke of Wei with the temple name Zhongding and given the ranks of chief minister of the Henan Branch Secretariat and Pillar of the State.

When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted Meritorious Minister for Loyalty, Integrity, and Preservation of Integrity; Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; chief minister of the Henan Branch Secretariat; and Pillar of the State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with the posthumous name Zhongding.
諡忠定 is a posthumous name (shi), not a temple name, and the Chinese also grants 宣忠守正保節功臣 and 榮祿大夫 omitted in the before text.
Angxiao was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Longxi with the temple name Zhongyi and honored as Minister of Rites.

Angxiao was posthumously granted Meritorious Minister for Sincerity, Filial Piety, and Integrity; Grand Master for Glorious Discussion; Minister of Rites; and Superior Commandant of Light Chariots; posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Longxi Commandery, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.
諡忠毅 is a posthumous name, not a temple name; the before text also drops 推誠孝節功臣、嘉議大夫、上輕車都尉 and the 郡 in 隴西郡侯.
In Zhizheng 3 (1343) Wu Ruqi and other rebels in Wan'an Army raised three thousand men in revolt.
In Zhiyuan 3 (1337) Wu Ruqi and other rebels in Wan'an Army raised three thousand men in revolt.
After 元統元年, 至元三年 is the later Zhiyuan year 3 (AD 1337), not Zhizheng 3 (AD 1343).
Following Liu Ji's counsel, Yisun alternated force and stratagem; soon every bandit band was wiped out.
Yisun used the plans of Ji and the others—sometimes striking with troops, sometimes luring with stratagems—and before long all were wiped out without survivors.
基等謀 means the plans of Ji and the others; attributing counsel to Liu Ji alone drops 等.
The court posthumously honored him as Duke of Yue with the temple name Zhongmin and granted him the ranks of Grand Academician and Supreme Pillar of the State.

When the matter was reported, the court posthumously granted him Meritorious Minister for Sincerity, Proclamation of Power, and Loyal Service, Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Supreme Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Yue, with the posthumous name Zhongmin.
諡忠愍 is a posthumous name, not a temple name, and the before text omits 推誠宣力效節功臣、集賢大學士、榮祿大夫 present in the Chinese.

Pacification Commissioner Puyan Buhua and the surveillance officials petitioned for state mourning honors, noting, "He would not eat rebel grain and starved at Qinquan—conduct worthy of Bo Yi and Shu Qi, the purity of a loyal minister."

Pacification Commissioner Puyan Buhua and the surveillance officials petitioned for state mourning honors; someone said, "He would not eat rebel grain and starved at Qinquan—conduct worthy of Bo Yi and Shu Qi, the purity of a loyal minister."
有曰 introduces an unnamed appraisal after the petition notice; the before text wrongly makes the quoted praise the petitioners' own noting.
He appointed Liu Ji director of his staff, Su Youlong registrar, and recruited local men Hu Shen, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi as military advisers.

He also appointed the Jiang-Zhe vice promoter of Confucian learning Liu Ji as director of his bureau and the Xiaoshan magistrate Su Youlong as registrar, while Yisun further recruited the men of his prefecture Hu Shen, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi to advise on military affairs.
又以…為 continues Dash Timur's appointments to 其院, while 宜孫又辟 marks Yisun's separate recruitment; collapsing both under one subject and dropping prior offices is inaccurate.
Promoted to director of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission, he remained at Shaoxing to guard the Secretariat with his troops.
Promoted to registrar of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission, he remained at Shaoxing to guard the Secretariat with his troops.
廉訪司經歷 is the commission's registrar/executive secretary, not its director.
He was promoted to director of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission, yet remained at Shaoxing, using troops to guard the Secretariat seat.
He was promoted to registrar of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission, yet remained at Shaoxing, using troops to guard the Secretariat seat.
Same office error in the literal field: 經歷 is registrar, not director.
